claims.claim: Visa publishes its U.S. interchange reimbursement fee schedule as a public PDF; the current edition is dated 18 April 2026 with rates effective April 18, 2026.
claims.quote: The following tables set forth the interchange reimbursement fees applied on Visa financial transactions completed within the 50 United States and the District of Columbia.
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: PDF saved by WebFetch; text extracted with pypdf. Cover: 'Visa Public'. 28 pages. Introduction states it is a supplement to the Visa Core Rules.

claims.claim: U.S. exempt (non-regulated) consumer debit CPS/Retail card-present interchange is 0.80% + $0.15; regulated debit is 0.05% + $0.21 (plus $0.01 for issuers certifying fraud-prevention compliance).
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table A, Rates Effective April 18, 2026. Footnote: 'Issuers that certify to Visa their compliance with the interim fraud prevention standards will receive an additional US $0.01.'

claims.claim: U.S. exempt debit CPS/Supermarket is a flat $0.30 and CPS/Small Ticket debit is 1.55% + $0.04; the default Standard debit rate is 1.90% + $0.25.
claims.quote: Standard Interchange Reimbursement Fee, Debit 1.90% + $0.25 0.05% + $0.21*
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same table also lists 'CPS/Supermarket, Debit $0.30' and 'CPS/Small Ticket, Debit 1.55% + $0.04'.

claims.claim: U.S. consumer credit card-present Retail (Performance Threshold I) interchange ranges from 1.43% + $0.10 for Traditional/All Other products to 2.30% + $0.10 for Visa Infinite Spend Qualified.
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table C columns in order: Visa Infinite Spend Qualified, Visa Infinite Spend Not Qualified, Visa Signature Preferred, Visa Signature, Traditional Rewards, All Other Products.

claims.claim: The highest published U.S. consumer credit rate is Non-Qualified Consumer Credit at 3.15% + $0.10 across all products; Restaurant card-present is 2.60% (min $0.04) for premium products and 2.10% for others.
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Visa offers published card-not-present interchange incentives of -0.05% (EMV token), -0.10% (Digital Commerce Authentication Program) and -0.15% (DCAP plus token) on qualifying consumer credit.
claims.quote: EMV Token transactions qualify for Card Not Present Incentive Type 1, except for Charity 1 and CPS/Utility.
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table C: 'Type 1 -0.05%', 'Type 2 -0.10%', 'Type 3 -0.15%'; 'Card Not Present Incentives require CPS qualification and are subject to change.'

claims.claim: Visa's U.S. Small Merchant credit interchange program applies to merchants with gross Visa consumer credit sales of no more than $280,000 (12 months ending September 30, 2024).
claims.quote: Gross Visa Consumer Credit Sales ** $280,000
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Small Merchant Product 2 rate for All Other Products is 1.29% + $0.10. Footnote refers to the 'U.S. Interchange Reimbursement Fee Rate Qualification Guide', which is not published on the page.

claims.claim: Large-merchant credit Performance Threshold I (Retail) requires at least 133.4 million transactions and $8.83 billion volume with a dispute ratio of at most 0.020% and PCI compliance.
claims.quote: Threshold I 133.4 million $8.83 billion 0.020%
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table D, 'Effective April 18, 2026, based on 12 months of activity ending September 30, 2025'. Supermarket Tier 0 requires 525.0 million transactions and $27.60 billion.

claims.claim: U.S. commercial (purchasing and corporate T&E) interchange runs from 1.75% + $0.10 (Commercial Product 3) to 2.95% + $0.10 (Non-Qualified); Commercial Product Large Ticket is 1.30% + $35.00.
claims.quote: Commercial Product Large Ticket 1.30% + $35.00
claims.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements, 18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table E. Also 'GSA Large Ticket 1.20% + $39.00' (Purchasing only).

claims.claim: Interlink (Visa's PIN debit network) publishes its own U.S. interchange schedule; exempt consumer Retail is 0.80% + $0.15, exempt Business Interlink 1.70% + $0.10, regulated 0.05% + $0.21, with rates effective July 1, 2023.
claims.title: Interlink Interchange Reimbursement Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: PDF metadata dates August 2023; 'Rates Effective July 1, 2023'. Older than the Visa USA schedule (April 2026). 'Balance inquiries, preauthorizations, and declines have no interchange fees applied to them.'

claims.claim: Visa states that merchants do not pay interchange directly; they pay a negotiated merchant discount to their acquirer, and merchants must give their acquirer 30 days' notice before surcharging credit.
claims.quote: Merchants must notify their acquirer 30 days before they begin surcharging.
claims.title: Regulations & Fees | Visa
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page also links the Visa USA and Interlink interchange PDFs and surcharging FAQ/considerations PDFs.

claims.claim: The public Visa Core Rules define an interchange reimbursement fee as a default transfer price between acquirers and issuers, with merchant pricing set independently by each acquirer.
claims.quote: An Interchange Reimbursement Fee is a default transfer price between Acquirers and Issuers within the Visa system.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 923-page public PDF; passage on p.128 of the PDF. Also: 'Interchange is consistently monitored and adjusted – sometimes increased and sometimes decreased'.

claims.claim: Visa's network (scheme) fees are set out in regional Fee Schedules that the public rulebook only names (Visa U.S.A., Canada, Asia-Pacific, CEMEA, LAC, and Visa Europe Non-EEA / Non-Regulated / Scheme); the schedules themselves are not published.
claims.quote: Fee Schedule One of the following: l Visa Asia-Pacific Fee Schedule l Visa Canada Fee Schedule l Visa CEMEA Fee Schedule
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (18 April 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Glossary p.859. Rule 12.6.3.1 says the investigative service fee is 'as specified in the applicable Fee Schedule'. No public copy of any Visa Fee Schedule was found.

claims.claim: Visa Canada publicly discloses its standard acquiring network assessment fees: an Acquirer Service Fee of 0.09% on all Canadian-acquired Visa volume, plus an International Acquirer Service Fee of 0.60% (multicurrency) or 1.00% (single-currency) on foreign-issued cards.
claims.quote: The Acquirer Service Fee rate is 0.09%
claims.title: Visa Canada Standard Acquiring Network Assessment Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'Multicurrency Purchase: 0.60%' and 'Single-Currency Purchase: 1.00%'. Document notes the 'Visa Fee Schedule' governs on any discrepancy. The only public network-fee (as opposed to interchange) figures found for Visa in this research.

claims.claim: Visa Canada manages domestic consumer credit interchange to an average of 1.40% under a voluntary commitment with the Canadian Department of Finance, with annual third-party validation.
claims.quote: a voluntary commitment with the Canadian Department of Finance that manages domestic consumer credit interchange rates to an average level of 1.40%
claims.title: Interchange | Visa Canada
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page states rate changes must comply with the notice requirements of the Code of Conduct for the Credit and Debit Card Industry in Canada (FCAC).

claims.claim: Visa Canada's published domestic consumer credit interchange for Electronic (card-present) transactions is 1.25% (Classic/Gold/Platinum), 1.57% (Infinite), 1.60% (Infinite+) and 2.08% (Infinite Privilege); Visa Debit Electronic is CA$0.03 per transaction.
claims.title: Visa Canada Interchange Reimbursement Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Debit table: 'Electronic $0.03 CAD per transaction', 'Standard 1.15%'. Performance Program requires 'Minimum of $2.3 billion in total net VisaNet retail sales volume in Canada'. No effective date printed on the PDF.

claims.claim: Visa Canada's international interchange table publishes Visa Direct-related and ATM economics: an Original Credit Transaction earns US$0.29 and OCT Fast Funds Delivery US$0.60; ATM cash disbursement interchange (issuer to acquirer) is $0.65 + 0.52% where no access fee is charged.
claims.quote: Original Credit Transaction (OCT) $0.29USD
claims.title: Visa Canada Interchange Reimbursement Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also 'OCT Fast Funds Delivery $0.60USD' and 'ATM Access Fee Free Service $0.65 + 0.52%'. Applies to Canadian-acquired transactions on cards issued outside Canada.

claims.claim: Effective 24 October 2026, Visa Canada will raise the Small Merchant Interchange Program volume ceiling from CAD 300,000 to CAD 750,000 and introduce a Digital Commerce Authentication Program (DCAP) with lower CNP rates, e.g. 1.30% for Classic/Gold/Platinum CNP-DCAP.
claims.quote: Visa will expand the Small Merchant Interchange Program by increasing the annual maximum Visa volume threshold criteria from CAD 300,000 to CAD 750,000.
claims.title: Visa Canada Upcoming Interchange Modifications
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Dated September 4, 2026; 'Domestic Consumer Credit Interchange Changes Effective CPD 24 October 2026'. Business Standard moves to 2.15%.

claims.claim: Visa Europe publishes per-country and intra-EEA interchange schedules and states that Visa itself receives none of the interchange fee; EEA consumer rates are capped by the IFR (Regulation (EU) 2015/751) since 9 December 2015.
claims.quote: Visa doesn't receive any of this fee.
claims.title: Fees and interchange | Visa Europe
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page links PDFs for 31 countries/territories plus inter-EEA and intra-EEA schedules (versions dated April 2025, November 2025, January 2026, May 2026).

claims.claim: Intra-EEA consumer interchange is 0.20% (debit/prepaid) and 0.30% (credit/deferred debit), while uncapped commercial rates run higher, e.g. Visa Business Debit at 1.30% (EMV chip) and 1.65% (e-commerce/standard).
claims.quote: Visa Business Debit EMV Chip (Incl. Contactless) 1.30% 1.30% (capped at €1.50) 1.30% (capped at €0.50)
claims.title: Intra Europe EEA | Multi-lateral Interchange Fees (April 2025)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Consumer column shows '0.20%', '0.20%', '0.30%'. Columns: General / Government Payments and Money Services (capped €1.50) / Charity (capped €0.50). Large Ticket Program 1: '1.00% + €60.00'.

claims.claim: UK domestic Visa commercial interchange (Feb 2026 schedule) is 0.75% card-present and 1.20% card-not-present for Visa Business Debit, rising to 1.75%/2.00% for Visa Purchasing, with a 2.05% non-qualified rate.
claims.quote: Visa Business Debit Card Present - EMV® (Incl. Contactless) 0.75% 0.75% (capped at £2.50)
claims.title: United Kingdom | Domestic Multi-lateral Interchange Fees (Feb 2026)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Visa Australia publishes domestic interchange with effective dates per product: consumer credit rates effective 1 June 2026 include Standard 0.220% and Super Premium (Visa Signature) 0.847% inclusive of GST; card-present standard debit is 4.4 cents.
claims.quote: Effective 1 June 2026, the following interchange rates apply to domestic transactions processed through Visa's NNSS
claims.title: Interchange | Visa Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Figures seen on page: Standard '0.220%', Government '0.198%', Supermarket '0.253%', Super Premium '0.847%', High Net Worth '0.869%'; debit Card Present Standard '4.4 cents', Premium '11.0 cents'. Multi-network debit effective 12 July 2025; single-network debit 1 December 2025.

claims.claim: For foreign cards issued outside Asia Pacific used at Australian merchants, Visa publishes inter-regional interchange of 1.10% (Classic/Gold consumer credit), 1.85% (premium consumer credit) and 2.00% (all commercial); no effective date is shown.
claims.title: Inter-regional Interchange Rates | Visa Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Other figures seen: '1.85%' premium consumer credit (alternative fee program), '2.00%' all commercial products. Same 1.10% / 1.85% / 2.00% structure appears in Visa Canada's international table.

claims.claim: Visa Developer Center pricing is tiered: sandbox use is free, a few APIs are free in production, some are bundled with a Visa Online subscription, and most are priced on usage (transactions, alerts, disputes, tokens, accounts enrolled).
claims.quote: Pricing for most capabilities is based on usage.
claims.title: Visa Developer Pricing
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'A few capabilities are currently available for use in production free of charge.' and 'APIs for certain capabilities are available for no additional fee if the client has a subscription for the capability through Visa Online.' No per-API price list is published.

claims.claim: Usage-priced Visa Developer APIs usually carry a monthly minimum per product, and going live requires a contract that includes flat setup fees for support and compliance checks; specific fees are quoted case by case.
claims.quote: There is usually a minimum fee per month (separate for each product) if the threshold of calls, accounts, etc. is not met.
claims.title: Visa Developer Pricing
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Setup: 'a flat setup fees to cover the support costs and any other required additional compliance checks'. Disclaimer: 'this information does not constitute a promise of a specific fee structure or discount for any particular case'.

claims.claim: The Visa Developer Going Live page routes developers to a general Pricing Guide and to 'Contact Us' for specific pricing and a contract; production credentials are released only once Visa approves and a signed contract is in place.
claims.quote: take a look at our Pricing Guide for general information
claims.title: Going Live | Visa Developer
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'Once you determine which product(s) you want to commercialize in your project, Contact Us for a contract.' Names the Onboarding Dashboard and Visa Developer Platform.

claims.claim: Visa Acceptance Solutions (formerly Cybersource) offers a free sandbox but publishes no pricing; the Cybersource pricing URL resolves to a contact-sales form.
claims.quote: Sign up for a free sandbox account
claims.title: Visa Acceptance Developer Center
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: https://www.cybersource.com/en-us/pricing.html redirected to https://www.cybersource.com/en-us/contact-us/sales.html ('please complete this request form'). Names Visa Acceptance Portal and Enterprise Business Center.

claims.claim: Visa's licensing page acknowledges that Principal clients pay required service fees but publishes no amounts; prospective members are directed to regional licensing teams.
claims.quote: While there are service fees that are required, these clients have the most flexibility for the capabilities they are able to manage
claims.title: Visa Licensing Program | Visa Partner
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Names Visa Access, Visa Client Lifecycle Management Tool and Visa Partner Portal. Consistent with 10-K 'Other revenue' including 'fees for account holder services, certification and licensing'.

claims.claim: Fintech Fast Track is marketed with cost benefits (free trials on select solutions, preferred terms with referral partners) but no fee waivers, pricing or incentive amounts are published.
claims.quote: free trials on select solutions, and preferred terms with Visa's select network of referral partners
claims.title: Fintech Fast Track | Visa Partner
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: usa.visa.com/partner-with-us/fintech-fast-track.html returned 404; program now lives on partner.visa.com.

claims.claim: Visa Inc. reports gross revenue in four lines and nets client incentives against them; fiscal 2025 client incentives were $15,751 million against net revenue of $40,000 million.
claims.quote: Client incentives (15,751)
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K FY2025 - Revenue - Schedule of Disaggregation of Revenue (Details)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: XBRL R-page rendered as a table (USD millions). FY2025: Service revenue 17,539; Data processing revenue 19,993; International transaction revenue 14,166; Other revenue 4,053; Client incentives (15,751); Net revenue 40,000. FY2024 incentives (13,764); FY2023 (12,297).

claims.claim: Visa's 10-K defines client incentives as payments to financial institutions, sellers and other partners to grow volume and acceptance, and 'Other revenue' as including license fees for the Visa brand and fees for certification and licensing.
claims.quote: Paid to financial institution clients, sellers and other business partners to grow payments volume; increase Visa product acceptance
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Other revenue: 'license fees for use of the Visa brand or technology; and fees for account holder services, certification and licensing'. International transaction revenue: 'Earned for cross-border transaction processing and currency conversion activities'. Full document truncated by WebFetch; curl blocked by SEC automated-tool filter.

claims.claim: The 2019 Amended Settlement Agreement in the U.S. interchange MDL received final approval on December 13, 2019; the March 25, 2024 injunctive-relief settlement was denied preliminary approval on June 25, 2024.
claims.quote: On March 25, 2024, Visa and Mastercard entered into a settlement agreement to resolve the Injunctive Relief Class claims.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K FY2025 - Legal Matters
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'On December 13, 2019, the district court granted final approval of the Amended Settlement Agreement, which was subsequently appealed.' and 'motion for preliminary approval of the settlement, which was denied on June 25, 2024.'

claims.claim: On November 10, 2025 Visa and Mastercard entered a superseding and amended injunctive-relief settlement with U.S. merchants; the court granted preliminary approval on June 9, 2026 and plaintiffs moved for final approval on July 15, 2026.
claims.quote: On November 10, 2025, Visa and Mastercard entered into a superseding and amended settlement agreement to resolve the Injunctive Relief Class claims
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 30, 2026 - Legal Matters
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'On July 15, 2026, the Injunctive Relief Class plaintiffs filed a motion for final approval of the settlement.' The note does not state the economic terms (rate reductions, caps, duration); see not_found.

claims.claim: As of June 30, 2026 Visa had settled with opt-out merchants representing about 95% of Visa-branded volume of merchants who opted out of the damages class, up from about 82% reported in the FY2025 10-K.
claims.quote: Visa has reached settlements with a number of merchants representing approximately 95% of the Visa-branded payment card sales volume
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 30, 2026 - Legal Matters
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 10-K FY2025 (R30) wording: 'approximately 82% of the Visa-branded payment card sales volume of merchants who opted out of the Amended Settlement Agreement'.

claims.claim: European interchange litigation continues to shape Visa's fee exposure: on April 20, 2026 a group of merchants from across Europe sued several Visa entities in the UK High Court alleging interchange restricts competition.
claims.quote: On April 20, 2026, a group of merchants from across Europe filed a claim in the UK High Court against several Visa entities
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 30, 2026 - Legal Matters
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: R69 details: U.K. Merchant Litigation 1,200 plaintiffs, 950 settled, 100 pending; litigation provision $1,290 million for nine months ended June 30, 2026; $875 million deposited into the U.S. litigation escrow.

claims.claim: The DOJ's September 24, 2024 Sherman Act complaint alleges Visa carries more than 60% of U.S. debit transactions and charges over $7 billion a year in fees on them, with North America operating margins of 83%.
claims.quote: more than 60% of debit transactions run on Visa's debit network, allowing it to charge over $7 billion in fees each year
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Allegations, not adjudicated findings. Also: 'Visa earns more in revenue from its U.S. debit business than its credit business as of 2022.' Court denied Visa's motion to dismiss on June 23, 2025 (per DOJ case page and Visa 10-K).

claims.claim: The DOJ complaint describes Visa's acquirer-side debit pricing as per-transaction network fees plus, since 2012, a fixed monthly Fixed Acquirer Network Fee (FANF) based on merchant locations and CNP volume, which Visa has raised twice.
claims.quote: Starting in 2012, Visa also began charging each merchant's acquirer a fixed monthly fee, known as the Fixed Acquirer Network Fee (FANF)
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'Visa has raised FANF twice in subsequent years.' and that FANF was introduced 'in response to threats of increased competition once the Durbin Amendment went into effect.' No public FANF schedule was found on Visa's site.

claims.claim: The DOJ alleges Visa's debit routing contracts use 'cliff pricing' (all-unit volume commitments) under which missing a committed threshold triggers Visa's published rack rates on all transactions, and cites a $20 million exclusivity payment to one merchant in 2023.
claims.quote: Visa's volume requirements are structured as cliff pricing.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'in 2023, Visa paid one large merchant over $20 million for exclusivity' and Visa 'charges punitively expensive rack rates (listed pricing for network fees and interchange)'. Allegations only.

claims.claim: Under Regulation II the debit interchange cap for covered issuers is $0.21 plus 0.05% of value plus a $0.01 fraud-prevention adjustment; in 2024 the all-network average interchange was $0.23 on covered and $0.51 on exempt transactions.
claims.title: Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Row columns: exempt (% of number, % of value, avg value, avg fee, fee as % of value), covered (same), all. Cap wording on page: '$0.21 plus 0.05 percent multiplied by the value of the transaction, plus a $0.01 fraud-prevention adjustment, if eligible'. WebFetch summary of the same table gave dual-message covered $0.22, single-message covered $0.24, exempt dual-message $0.61, exempt single-message $0.26 (row text not captured verbatim). Page last updated December 19, 2025.

claims.claim: In October 2023 the Federal Reserve proposed lowering the Reg II cap so that a $50 debit transaction would carry 17.7 cents instead of 24.5 cents, with biennial updates thereafter.
claims.quote: 24.5 cents under the current rule
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on a proposal to lower the maximum interchange fee that a large debit card issuer can receive
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also '17.7 cents under the proposal'. Fed's Reg II overview page (updated May 17, 2024) still lists the proposal as open; no final rule or court status was found on Fed pages (see not_found).

claims.claim: The UK PSR's final report (6 March 2025) found Mastercard and Visa raised core scheme and processing fees to acquirers by at least 25% since 2017, costing UK businesses at least £170 million a year, in a market without effective competition.
claims.quote: Mastercard and Visa increased their core scheme and processing fees to acquirers by at least 25% since 2017
claims.title: MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme and processing fees: final report
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also 'costing businesses at least £170million extra per year'. Hub page: 'Mastercard and Visa don't face competition with fees rising and a lack of clarity on how much businesses will have to pay'.

claims.claim: The PSR's PS26/1 final decision (30 July 2026) imposes an Information, Transparency and Complexity Direction and a Pricing Governance Direction on Visa and Mastercard; pricing-governance duties apply from end November 2026 and ITC duties from end July 2027.
claims.quote: Relevant fee decisions must comply with the Pricing Governance Direction from end of November 2026
claims.title: PS26/1 Market review of card scheme and processing fees: final decision on ITC remedy and pricing governance remedy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Implemented via Specific Directions 22 and 23; a regulatory financial reporting direction was under consultation (CP26/1).

claims.claim: The PSR found Visa and Mastercard raised UK-EEA card-not-present consumer cross-border interchange from 0.2%/0.3% to 1.15%/1.5% after Brexit, costing UK businesses £150-200 million a year, and in October 2025 chose not to impose an interim cap while consulting on a long-term cap methodology.
claims.quote: 0.2% and 0.3% to 1.15% and 1.5% respectively
claims.title: Market review into cross-border interchange fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Final report MR22/2.7 (October 2025). 'The increases are costing businesses £150-200 million extra annually.' Interim cap not pursued 'due to ongoing litigation regarding its powers'; consultation MR22/2.8 on price cap methodology.

claims.claim: The European Commission's 2020 IFR review found interchange fell and merchant service charges dropped after the caps, while scheme fees (outside the IFR) rose to a limited extent, mainly at international schemes; estimated consumer savings EUR 864-1,930 million a year.
claims.quote: Scheme fees, which are not within the scope of the IFR, appear to have increased to a limited extent
claims.title: Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2020) 118 final: Report on the application of Regulation (EU) 2015/751 on interchange fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'estimated annual consumer cost savings of between EUR 864 million and EUR 1,930 million'. Quote whitespace normalised from PDF extraction ('increased to a limited extent ,').

claims.claim: The RBA's 31 March 2026 conclusions cut Australian consumer credit interchange cap to 0.3% (from 0.8%), keep debit at 8 cents benchmark and cap, add a cap on foreign-issued cards, end surcharging from 1 October 2026, and require networks to publish interchange and scheme fees; estimated wholesale savings around $910 million a year.
claims.quote: An interchange cap of 0.3 per cent will significantly reduce the extent to which small merchants cross-subsidise large merchants by paying higher interchange rates.
claims.title: Review of Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging - Conclusions Paper (31 March 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'retain the debit interchange benchmark at 8 cents per transaction and to reduce the cap only to 8 cents per transaction'; 'lowering wholesale card payment costs for merchants by around $910 million per year'; networks must 'publish their interchange and scheme fees, reduce the complexity of their scheme fees and justify any increases'. Hub page: surcharging ends 1 October 2026; foreign-card cap from 1 April 2027. Average consumer credit interchange was 0.47% with small merchants at up to 0.8% and largest merchants as low as 0.18%.

claims.claim: Visa Direct's product page publishes no pricing; prospective partners are sent to a sales form, and Visa Developer's pricing page indicates such capabilities are priced on usage under contract.
claims.quote: Connect with our team
